items.label: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q3 FY2026 (05-06-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Memory shortage impact on PCs and smartphones (CEO Stephen Chang)

set.signal: Memory shortage impact on PCs and smartphones (CEO Stephen Chang): memory supply constraints and price pressures 'represent growing headwinds for the second half of calendar 2026'. In PCs, some customers are building out sooner to get products out, and there is 'a lot of uncertainty about the second half'; AOS expects some decline in the PC market in calendar 2026 but believes it should outpace the market on BOM content from its total solutions on next-generation platforms such as Intel's Panther Lake. In smartphones, AOS is prioritizing capacity for its Tier 1 U.S. smartphone customers and premium models, which it expects to be more resilient to memory shortages, and increasing charging currents let it introduce new higher-ASP products; it still expects continued smartphone growth in calendar 2026. In the June-quarter computing outlook the CEO said PC-related revenue is largely stable while 'tablets declined mostly due to seasonality as well as increased capacity allocation to opportunities in smartphones'.

items.reason: The tablet remark is stated in the past tense inside the June-quarter outlook ('tablets declined'); the entry rewrote it as a June-quarter forecast ('were expected to decline'). Quote it as said instead of inferring the tense.
items.evidence: Looking ahead to the June quarter, we expect computing segment revenue to increase ... While PC-related revenue is largely stable, tablets declined mostly due to seasonality as well as increased capacity allocation to opportunities in smartphones.
